Jonas,

Hope you’re well. We added 12 seats (intent to scale quickly) on Aug 10, but our AP team just flagged a charge on the Aug invoice that looks like a full-month seat fee for those seats rather than a pro-rated amount. Can you confirm how Redwood handled the mid-cycle charge and provide a breakdown?

I can attach our PO and the invoice PDF if that helps — happy to share any usage timestamps. We need a corrected invoice for our internal reconciliation (and VAT handling) if this was billed at the full month.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Unexpected partial-month seat charges — can you help?

Alex — thanks for flagging. Apologies for the confusion; I want to get a clean answer for your AP team. Two quick items so we calculate correctly:

1) Can you confirm the exact activation timestamp for the 12 seats (you mentioned Aug 10) — timezone ok?
2) Do you prefer a corrected invoice (credit + reissue) or an account credit/voucher for the pro-rated difference? Our usual flow is credit + reissue when PO numbers must match.

I’ve looped in Laura (billing) to run the proration calc and handle VAT nuances. If you can drop the PO and the current invoice as attachments, we’ll generate: (A) a proration breakdown, (B) a provisional corrected invoice, and (C) a DocuSign amendment if you need the PO/term referenced.

Quick note on approach: we prorate daily by seat-day for mid-cycle activations. If seats were active for 21 of 31 days in Aug we’ll bill 21/31 of the seat monthly price, plus VAT where applicable. Laura will include line-level detail.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2026 08:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected partial-month seat charges — proration breakdown and provisional invoice

Hi Alex — attaching the proration workbook and a provisional corrected invoice for Aug. Summary below:

- Activation timestamp used: 2026-08-10T09:14:00-07:00 (confirmed by deployment logs supplied by your team).
- Plan: Team Pro — seat price $200/month, VAT at 8% (Sunrise EU VAT registered? you previously noted a US entity — we treated as US taxable for now).
- Proration calculation (per seat): billed days = 22 (10th inclusive to 31st), month length = 31 -> 22/31 * $200 = $141.94 per seat.
- Charge posted on original invoice: billed as full seat ($200) for 12 seats = $2,400.
- Correct pro-rated charge should have been: 12 * $141.94 = $1,703.28.
- Net difference: $696.72 (to be credited). VAT impact: if taxed, additional VAT adjustments required on the credit/reissue.

Options we propose:
A) Issue a credit for $696.72 and reissue corrected invoice for $1,703.28 (+VAT if applicable).
B) Apply $696.72 as account credit/voucher to be consumed against Sep charges (no invoice reissue).

Per Alex’s note about reconciliation, option A is recommended if you need PO/invoice numbers to match. I attached: invoice_202608_prorated.pdf (provisional reissue), proration_breakdown_202608.csv (line-level math). Also added a DocuSign amendment link we can send to your procurement if you need the seat add timeline appended to the order.

Laura Bennett
Billing Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachments: invoice_202608_prorated.pdf, proration_breakdown_202608.csv, amendment_docusign_link.txt
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Unexpected partial-month seat charges — next steps on credit vs voucher

Quick operational note: finance can create either a credit memo (recommended for audit trails) or an account voucher. If you need the credit memo to reference PO# SB-4579 we can add that on issuance.

If you confirm option A (credit + reissue), we’ll: (1) raise credit memo CM-202608-4821, (2) post corrected invoice INV-202608-RD-4821, and (3) copy your AP contact on both documents. Expect turnaround ~2 business days after confirmation.

If you choose option B (voucher), the credit will post to your account and appear on the next statement — no reissued invoice. That’s faster but less explicit for PO matching.

Let me know which you prefer and we’ll action.

Ben Carter
Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
